# Facts That Change {#sec-facts}

```{python}
#| label: facts-setup
from IPython.display import Markdown

from scripts.facts import all_items, table


def cell(text: str) -> str:
    """Text for a table cell: no line breaks, no stray pipes."""
    return " ".join(str(text).split()).replace("|", "\\|")


def dollars(x: float) -> str:
    """A price as Chapter 2 prints it: 50, or 0.50."""
    return f"{x:g}" if x == int(x) else f"{x:.2f}"


def sources(e: dict) -> str:
    urls = [e["url"], *e.get("also", [])]
    if len(urls) == 1:
        return f"[source]({urls[0]})"
    return "sources " + ", ".join(f"[{i + 1}]({u})" for i, u in enumerate(urls))
```

Prices, plans, accounts and free allowances change from month to month, so this book keeps
them in one place: a file in its source, `book/facts.yml`, which this appendix prints in full.
The chapters quote it rather than typing a price or a plan, so when a fact changes, one edit
and a rebuild update every page that mentions it, and this list. Each fact carries the date it
was checked against the official page linked beside it. By the time you read this, some will
have changed: follow the link, and trust the page over the book.

```{python}
#| output: asis
# One section per group of facts, each fact a short paragraph: a table of four columns does
# not fit a phone's width.
sections = {}
for title, key, e in all_items():
    sections.setdefault(title, []).append(e)
for title, entries in sections.items():
    print(f"## {title} {{.unnumbered}}\n")
    for e in entries:
        text = cell(e["text"])
        print(f"**{cell(e['label'])}.** {text[0].upper() + text[1:]}. Checked {e['checked']}, "
              f"{sources(e)}.\n")
```

## Model prices {.unnumbered}

```{python}
#| output: asis
prices = table("models", "prices")
rows = ["| Model | What the vendor says it is for | Input / output, \\$ per million tokens |",
        "|---|---|---|"]
for r in prices["rows"]:
    rows.append(f"| {r['model']} | \"{cell(r['for'])}\" | {dollars(r['input'])} / {dollars(r['output'])} |")
print("\n".join(rows))
print(f"\n: {prices['caption']}, checked {prices['checked']}. {{#tbl-prices}}")
print(f"\n{cell(prices['note'])} Sources: Anthropic's [pricing]({prices['url']}) and "
      f"[models]({prices['also'][0]}) pages and OpenAI's [models]({prices['also'][1]}) pages.")
```

These are *API* prices: what a program pays per token when it calls the model directly
(@sec-choose). Read them as a snapshot of the spread between small and large models, not as
numbers to plan with.

## Free plans for static sites {.unnumbered}

```{python}
#| output: asis
hosts = table("hosting", "hosts")
rows = ["| Host | Free plan |", "|---|---|"]
rows += [f"| [{h['host']}]({h['url']}) | {h['free']} |" for h in hosts["rows"]]
print("\n".join(rows))
print(f"\n: Free plans of six static hosts, checked on their official pages on {hosts['checked']}. {{#tbl-hosts-free}}")
```

@sec-hosting explains the two ways these hosts work: you render and upload, or they build
from your repository.
